turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because the doctor doing my insurance physical told me my weight was too low. I mean, they made a bit of a deal about it, but to me, I just look lean. I'm a painter, so I'm up and down ladders and working long days all the time, so it makes sense to me. But yeah, that's why they told me I needed to come see you.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient reports being referred after an insurance physical determined their body weight was too low.
symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient minimizes the clinical concern about their low weight, attributing it to work and viewing themselves as merely lean.

turns.doctor_question: What is your main reason for wanting to stay at your current weight or lose weight?
turns.patient_response: I guess it's just that... I really don't want it to go up. If I check the scale and it goes up even a little bit—like, maybe after a dinner with a client or if I eat something with bread—I get pretty tense about it. So I just start cutting back the next day to make sure the weight doesn't stick. I just prefer to keep things exactly where they are.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient reports becoming tense if the scale increases even slightly and cutting back food intake to prevent weight gain, demonstrating fear of gaining weight.

turns.doctor_question: When you look at your body, do you feel that you are overweight or need to lose weight even when other people tell you that you are very thin?
turns.patient_response: I wouldn't say I look at myself and think I'm massively overweight. But... I do fixate on certain things. Like, when I catch myself in a mirror, or if I'm looking at photos of myself standing next to one of my murals, I basically judge the whole day by whether my stomach and my face look sharp enough. If they don't look lean to me, then yeah, I feel like I need to trim down, regardless of what that insurance doctor or anyone else says.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient reports judging their entire day based on whether their stomach and face appear lean and sharp enough, and feeling the need to lose weight regardless of what doctors or others say, demonstrating an undue influence of body shape/weight on self-evaluation.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had an episode when you felt unable to control how much you were eating?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I don't think I've ever had a time where I felt like I couldn't stop or didn't have control over it. If anything, it's the exact opposite. I always know exactly how much I'm eating, and I keep a pretty tight handle on it.

symptom_reasoning.S050: The patient explicitly denies ever experiencing an episode where they felt unable to stop eating or lacked control over their eating.

turns.doctor_question: Has your weight been significantly below what is considered healthy for someone of your height and build?
turns.patient_response: Well, I guess that's actually why I'm here. I had to get a physical for my insurance, and the doctor there told me my weight was too low. He said it was below what's healthy for my height. I mean, I don't really see it that way. To me, I just look lean. I'm up and down ladders all day, working long hours painting, so it just makes sense that I'd be on the thinner side. But yeah, according to that doctor, it's significantly below where it should be.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient confirms that an insurance physical determined their weight is significantly below what is healthy for their height.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever deliberately made yourself vomit after eating?
turns.patient_response: No, I've never done that. I don't make myself throw up. Like I said, I just keep a close eye on what I eat to begin with, so I don't feel the need to do anything like that.

symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies ever engaging in self-induced vomiting or making themselves throw up after eating.
